group.title: Useful verbs
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To stay away from something or try not to do it.
examples: I {avoid} driving in the city at rush hour.
wrong: He avoided the shop by going there every day.

words.meaning: To annoy or disturb someone.
examples: Sorry to {bother} you, but can you help me?
wrong: The noise bothered him, so he felt calm and happy.

words.meaning: To make something happen, usually something bad.
examples: The storm {caused} a lot of damage.
wrong: The rain caused the fire to start.

words.meaning: To think carefully about something before deciding.
examples: We are {considering} moving to a bigger flat.
wrong: She considered the offer without thinking about it.

words.meaning: To have something inside.
examples: This box {contains} old photos.
wrong: The empty bottle contains a lot of water.

words.meaning: To become or make something bigger in number or size.
examples: The price of bread has {increased} again.
wrong: The number of students increased from fifty to ten.

words.meaning: To make something smaller or less.
examples: Turn off the lights to {reduce} your bills.
wrong: They reduced the price from ten dollars to twenty.

words.meaning: To earn something because of what you have done.
examples: You worked hard, so you {deserve} a rest.
wrong: He didn’t work at all, so he deserved the prize for hard work.

words.meaning: To grow or change into something bigger or better.
examples: The town {developed} into a big city.
wrong: The plant developed by getting smaller and dying.

words.meaning: To go out of sight or stop existing.
examples: The sun {disappeared} behind the clouds.
wrong: The cat disappeared and sat in front of us all day.

words.meaning: To think that something will probably happen.
examples: We {expect} the train to arrive at six.
wrong: I expected the rain, so I was very surprised by it.

words.meaning: To move something up to a higher position.
examples: Can you help me {lift} this heavy box?
wrong: He lifted the box by pushing it down to the floor.

words.meaning: To plan or mean to do something.
examples: I {intend} to finish this report today.
wrong: She intended to go, so she had no plan to go.

words.meaning: To succeed in doing something difficult.
examples: He {managed} to fix the car on his own.
wrong: She managed to open the door, but it stayed closed.

words.meaning: To see or become aware of something.
examples: Did you {notice} her new haircut?
wrong: I noticed the noise, but I didn’t hear anything.

words.meaning: To have something that belongs to you.
examples: They {own} a small house by the sea.
wrong: He owns the car, but it isn’t his.

words.meaning: To act as if something is true when it is not.
examples: He {pretended} to be asleep when Mom came in.
wrong: She pretended to be sick because she really was sick.

words.meaning: To give people something they need.
examples: The hotel {provides} towels and soap.
wrong: The school provides lunch, so students get no food.

words.meaning: To suddenly understand or become aware of something.
examples: I {realized} I had left my keys at home.
wrong: He realized the answer but still had no idea.

words.meaning: To know someone or something because you have seen it before.
examples: I didn’t {recognize} you with short hair.
wrong: I recognized the man I had never seen before.

words.meaning: To say you will not do or accept something.
examples: She {refused} to pay for the broken plate.
wrong: He refused the job and started work the next day.

words.meaning: To need and trust someone or something to help you.
examples: You can {rely} on me to be there.
wrong: I rely on him because he always lets me down.

words.meaning: To take something away from a place.
examples: Please {remove} your shoes before you come in.
wrong: He removed the picture by hanging it on the wall.

words.meaning: To put something new in the place of something old.
examples: I need to {replace} my broken phone.
wrong: He replaced the old battery by keeping it in.

words.meaning: To appear to be something.
examples: She {seems} tired today.
wrong: He seemed happy, so nobody could tell how he felt.

words.meaning: To divide things or people, or move them apart.
examples: {Separate} the eggs into yolks and whites.
wrong: She separated the two dogs by tying them together.

words.meaning: To move or reach a bigger area or more people.
examples: The news {spread} quickly around the school.
wrong: The fire spread and stayed in one small corner.

words.meaning: To think that something is probably true.
examples: I {suppose} you’re hungry after that long walk.
wrong: I suppose it’s true, so I’m sure it’s false.

words.meaning: To stay alive after a dangerous event.
examples: Everyone {survived} the crash.
wrong: Nobody survived, so all of them lived.

words.meaning: To usually do something or be likely to happen.
examples: I {tend} to wake up early.
wrong: He tends to be late, so he is never late.

words.meaning: To use more of something than you need, or use it badly.
examples: Don’t {waste} water; turn off the tap.
wrong: He wasted no time, so he was very slow.

words.meaning: To have a certain heaviness, or measure how heavy something is.
examples: The suitcase {weighs} twenty kilos.
wrong: She weighed the rope by measuring how long it was.

words.meaning: To cover something with paper or cloth.
examples: She {wrapped} the present in red paper.
wrong: He wrapped the gift by opening it.

words.meaning: To move something quickly up and down or side to side.
examples: {Shake} the bottle before you open it.
wrong: He shook the bottle by keeping it completely still.

words.meaning: To make a liquid flow out of a container.
examples: Can you {pour} me a glass of water?
wrong: She poured the bread into the toaster.

words.meaning: To make something curved, or move your body forward and down.
examples: {Bend} your knees when you lift heavy boxes.
wrong: He bent the stick so it stayed perfectly straight.

words.meaning: To pay no attention to someone or something.
examples: He {ignored} my question and kept walking.
wrong: She ignored him by listening carefully to every word.

words.meaning: To go or do something very quickly.
examples: We {rushed} to catch the last bus.
wrong: He rushed home, taking his time and walking slowly.

words.meaning: To do what a person, rule or law tells you.
examples: Drivers must {obey} the speed limit.
wrong: He obeyed the rule by breaking it.

words.meaning: To plan or organize something for the future.
examples: I’ve {arranged} a meeting for Monday.
wrong: She arranged the trip by making no plans at all.
